claims.text: The starting material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxidation resistance and undergoes pesting in high-temperature air.
High-temperature oxidation of untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr degrades its mechanical performance.
Pack cementation can deposit a thin aluminide coating on equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The aluminide coating will react with oxygen to form a dense, adherent, continuous Al2O3 scale.
The resulting alumina scale will grow slowly.
The continuous alumina scale will impede oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Impeded oxygen diffusion will mitigate oxidation and pesting.
A thin aluminide coating will not alter the bulk microstructure of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The bulk microstructure governs the mechanical properties of this alloy.
Relative to untreated material, aluminized specimens will have significantly lower oxygen uptake after 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
Relative to untreated material, aluminized specimens will develop a thinner oxide scale after 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
Aluminized specimens will retain the untreated alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility after oxidation exposure.
Aluminized specimens will retain the untreated alloy's near-1000 °C yield strength after oxidation exposure.
The proposed protection is applicable to as-cast material for exposure in air at temperatures up to 800 °C for 5 hours under low-to-moderate loading.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the treatment will preserve mechanical properties without degradation, but the falsification rule permits deterioration of up to 10% without falsifying that claim.
